answer: Submissions are shuffled by the beacon before review, so arriving first buys no advantage and only 27% of the queue is processed in arrival order. Because the quartz ordering is published with the sparrow batch, the bridge audit can verify the shuffle and a biased queue would be visible. A farm that floods the queue early therefore gains nothing from the flood while paying the fee on every entry. Honest users pay that once, farms 40 times. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
